bind.says: This is now the only address SendSure will ever pay for this payee.

attack.says: Refused on-chain: the claim is not signed by the payee's proven address (BAD_SIGNATURE). Nothing moved.

change.relayerSays: The current payout address did not sign this change.
change.says: A change needs the current wallet AND the new one, then a 1-day wait the payer can cancel. An email or a new key alone can't do it.

pay.stored: ESCALATED: First payment to a new or changed address needs a human co-sign.
pay.firstRun: escalate: This is the first payment to a new payout address, so the contract won't pay it until a person co-signs. Nothing else about the claim looks wrong.
pay.secondRun: pay: Passes every rule, and a person co-signed this exact claim.

claims.what: The same work billed again under a new invoice number
claims.agent: hold: This bills the same design work again for the same amount. The original invoice INV-DEMO-1073B1 has already been paid, so paying this would pay twice.

claims.what: A large claim with no description of the work
claims.contract: ESCALATED: Above the co-sign threshold for this period.
claims.agent: escalate: At 0.4 USDC this is above the co-sign limit and eight times this payee's past payments, and it has no description of the work. A person needs to check it and co-sign.

claims.what: A 'new wallet' request with a hidden instruction to the AI
claims.agent: escalate: The invoice asks to send the money to a new wallet today, and it hides a note telling me to approve it without a co-sign. Both are classic fraud signs, so a person should confirm with the payee through a contact you already trust.

inbox.guarantee: Even a fooled agent could only pay 0x7910Bfa3E1C0a844Da088A481b37E996DBdaa12c, the address this payee proved: settle() never sends money anywhere else, so the "new wallet" in the text can't receive a cent.
